in.answer_say: Went! Yesterday we went home.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai bentuk lampau: go jadi went.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “Yesterday I go to school.” 😅 Untuk kejadian kemarin, pakai bentuk lampau: “Yesterday I went to school.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “went”. Ceritakan harimu kemarin dengan went, ate, saw. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian does not change verbs, but English uses the past form: go becomes went.
en.caption: Ever say this? “Yesterday I go to school.” 😅 For yesterday, use the past form: “Yesterday I went to school.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: He is tall! Yes!

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “dia cantik” tanpa kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh is/am/are.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “She beautiful.” 😅 Jangan lupa is setelah she: “She is beautiful.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “He is tall.” Buat tiga kalimat pendek dengan is hari ini. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “dia cantik” has no verb, but English needs is, am or are.
en.caption: Ever say this? “She beautiful.” 😅 Do not forget is after she: “She is beautiful.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Pens! I have three pens.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia tidak menambah akhiran jamak, tapi bahasa Inggris menambah -s setelah angka lebih dari satu.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I have two book.” 😅 Dari dua ke atas, tambahkan s: “I have two books.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “pens”. Hitung benda di sekitarmu dan tambahkan s. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian has no plural ending, but English adds -s after a number above one.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I have two book.” 😅 With two or more, add s: “I have two books.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Say very much at the end.
in.answer_say: Like! I like music very much.

native.tip: “Saya sangat suka” tidak bisa diterjemahkan kata per kata. Pakai like ... very much.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I very like coffee.” 😅 Letakkan very much di akhir: “I like coffee very much.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “like”. Coba bilang “I like ... very much” untuk makananmu. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Saya sangat suka” cannot be translated word for word. Use like ... very much.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I very like coffee.” 😅 Put very much at the end: “I like coffee very much.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Are! Where are you going?

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “Kamu mau ke mana?” cukup singkat, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh are dan going.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “Where you go?” 😅 Tanyakan dengan lengkap: “Where are you going?” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “are”. Tanya temanmu: “Where are you going?” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “Kamu mau ke mana?” is short, but English needs are and going.
en.caption: Ever say this? “Where you go?” 😅 Ask the full question: “Where are you going?” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Ate! I already ate lunch.

native.tip: Kata “sudah” di bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai bentuk lampau: ate.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I already eat breakfast.” 😅 Untuk yang sudah selesai, pakai ate: “I already ate breakfast.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “ate”. Bilang “I already ate” saat ditanya sudah makan. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian “sudah” does not change the verb, but English uses the past form: ate.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I already eat breakfast.” 😅 For something done, use ate: “I already ate breakfast.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Is! My teacher is kind.

native.tip: Kita sering bilang “teman saya, dia baik”, tapi di bahasa Inggris subjek tidak diulang.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “My friend she is nice.” 😅 Subjek cukup disebut sekali: “My friend is nice.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “is”. Ceritakan temanmu tanpa kata she tambahan. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: We often say “teman saya, dia baik”, but English does not repeat the subject.
en.caption: Ever say this? “My friend she is nice.” 😅 Say the subject only once: “My friend is nice.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Are! There are many cars.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia pakai “ada” untuk satu atau banyak, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai there are untuk jamak.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “There is many people here.” 😅 Untuk banyak, pakai there are: “There are many people here.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “are”. Lihat sekitarmu dan bilang “There are ...” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian uses “ada” for one or many, but English uses there are for plural.
en.caption: Ever say this? “There is many people here.” 😅 For many, use there are: “There are many people here.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Bored! I am bored in class.

native.tip: Bosan = bored (perasaanmu). Membosankan = boring (hal yang bikin bosan). “I am boring” artinya “aku membosankan”!
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I am boring today.” 😅 Perasaanmu? Pakai bored: “I am bored today.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “bored”. Ingat: kamu bored, filmnya boring. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Bored = how you feel. Boring = a thing that makes you bored. “I am boring” means “I am a boring person”!
en.caption: Ever say this? “I am boring today.” 😅 Your feeling? Use bored: “I am bored today.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Can you borrow me your pen?
in.right: Can you lend me your pen?
in.answer_say: Lend! Can you lend me some money?

native.tip: “Pinjam” bisa berarti borrow atau lend. Minta orang meminjamkan? Pakai lend.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “Can you borrow me your pen?” 😅 Minta orang meminjamkan? Pakai lend: “Can you lend me your pen?” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “lend”. Minta temanmu meminjamkan sesuatu dengan lend. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Pinjam” can mean borrow or lend. Asking someone to lend you something? Use lend.
en.caption: Ever say this? “Can you borrow me your pen?” 😅 Asking someone to lend? Use lend: “Can you lend me your pen?” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I go to home after work.
in.answer_say: Go! I go home at night.

native.tip: Kita bilang “pulang ke rumah”, tapi di bahasa Inggris cukup go home, tanpa to.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I go to home after work.” 😅 Dengan home, tidak perlu to: “I go home after work.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “go”. Ucapkan “I go home” lima kali. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: We say “pulang ke rumah”, but in English it is just go home, with no to.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I go to home after work.” 😅 With home, you do not need to: “I go home after work.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I have lived here since two years.
in.right: I have lived here for two years.

quiz.stem: I have worked here ___ three years.

in.answer_say: For! I have worked here for three years.

native.tip: “Sejak dua tahun” bukan since two years. Untuk lamanya waktu pakai for; since untuk titik awal (since 2020).
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I have lived here since two years.” 😅 Untuk lamanya waktu, pakai for: “I have lived here for two years.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “for”. Ceritakan sudah berapa lama kamu belajar bahasa Inggris dengan for. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Not “since two years”. For is the length of time; since is the starting point (since 2020).
en.caption: Ever say this? “I have lived here since two years.” 😅 For a length of time, use for: “I have lived here for two years.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I have ever been to Bali.
in.answer_say: Have been! I have been to Bali.

native.tip: “Saya pernah ke Bali” cukup I have been to Bali. Ever dipakai di pertanyaan: Have you ever been to Bali?
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I have ever been to Bali.” 😅 Dalam kalimat biasa, buang ever: “I have been to Bali.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “have been”. Tanya temanmu: “Have you ever been to ...?” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Saya pernah ke Bali” is just I have been to Bali. Use ever in questions: Have you ever been to Bali?
en.caption: Ever say this? “I have ever been to Bali.” 😅 In a normal sentence, drop ever: “I have been to Bali.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Studying! I am studying now.

native.tip: “Saya sedang belajar” butuh am dan -ing di bahasa Inggris, bukan hanya study.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I study English now.” 😅 Untuk yang sedang terjadi, pakai am studying: “I am studying English now.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “studying”. Bilang apa yang sedang kamu lakukan sekarang. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Saya sedang belajar” needs am and -ing in English, not only study.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I study English now.” 😅 For right now, use am studying: “I am studying English now.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Has! He has a big house.

native.tip: Kata kerja bahasa Indonesia sama untuk semua orang, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai has setelah she dan he.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “She have a new car.” 😅 Setelah she atau he, pakai has: “She has a new car.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “has”. Ceritakan temanmu: “He has ...” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian verbs stay the same for everyone, but English uses has after she and he.
en.caption: Ever say this? “She have a new car.” 😅 After she or he, use has: “She has a new car.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Doesn't! She doesn't like tea.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia cukup pakai “tidak” untuk semua orang, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai doesn't setelah he dan she.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “He don't like fish.” 😅 Setelah he atau she, pakai doesn't: “He doesn't like fish.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “doesn't”. Bilang tiga hal yang temanmu tidak suka. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian uses “tidak” for everyone, but English uses doesn't after he and she.
en.caption: Ever say this? “He don't like fish.” 😅 After he or she, use doesn't: “He doesn't like fish.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Old! I am 30 years old.

native.tip: “25 tahun” saja belum cukup. Bilang “I am 25” atau “I am 25 years old”.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I am 25 years.” 😅 Untuk umur, tambahkan old: “I am 25 years old.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “old”. Sebutkan umurmu lengkap: “I am ... years old” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “25 tahun” alone is not enough. Say “I am 25” or “I am 25 years old”.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I am 25 years.” 😅 For your age, add old: “I am 25 years old.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Live! I live in a small town.

native.tip: Banyak yang mengira “I am” = “saya”. Padahal live sudah kata kerja: cukup I live.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I am live in Jakarta.” 😅 Cukup bilang I live: “I live in Jakarta.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “live”. Perkenalkan tempat tinggalmu: “I live in ...” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Many think “I am” = “saya”. But live is already a verb: just say I live.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I am live in Jakarta.” 😅 Just say I live: “I live in Jakarta.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I and my friend are late.
in.right: My friend and I are late.
in.answer_say: My sister and I! My sister and I are home.

native.tip: Kita bilang “saya dan teman saya”, jadi muncul “I and my friend”. Di bahasa Inggris, sebut diri sendiri terakhir: my friend and I.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I and my friend are late.” 😅 Sebut dirimu terakhir: “My friend and I are late.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “My sister and I”. Bilang “My friend and I” saat bercerita. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.hook: “I and my friend”? Flip the order
en.tip: We say “saya dan teman saya”, so “I and my friend” appears. In English, name yourself last: my friend and I.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I and my friend are late.” 😅 Name yourself last: “My friend and I are late.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Swim! I can swim well.

native.tip: Karena sering dengar “want to” dan “need to”, kita ikut menambah to. Setelah can, langsung kata kerja.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I can to swim.” 😅 Setelah can, langsung kata kerja: “I can swim.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “swim”. Bilang “I can ...” untuk tiga hal yang kamu bisa. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Because we often hear “want to” and “need to”, we add to too. After can, go straight to the verb.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I can to swim.” 😅 After can, use the verb directly: “I can swim.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: To! I want to eat.

native.tip: “Mau pulang” tidak butuh kata penghubung, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh to setelah want.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I want go home.” 😅 Setelah want, pakai to: “I want to go home.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “to”. Bilang “I want to ...” tiga kali hari ini. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Mau pulang” needs no linking word, but English needs to after want.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I want go home.” 😅 After want, use to: “I want to go home.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Let's! Let's eat now!

native.tip: “Ayo kita pergi” jadi let's we go, padahal let's = let us, sudah ada “kita”.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “Let's we go!” 😅 Let's sudah berarti let us, jadi cukup: “Let's go!” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “Let's”. Ajak temanmu dengan “Let's ...!” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Ayo kita pergi” becomes let's we go, but let's = let us, so “we” is already inside.
en.caption: Ever say this? “Let's we go!” 😅 Let's already means let us, so just say: “Let's go!” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Of! She is afraid of spiders.

native.tip: Kita bilang “takut dengan”, tapi di bahasa Inggris pakai afraid of.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I am afraid with dogs.” 😅 Untuk rasa takut, pakai of: “I am afraid of dogs.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “of”. Hafalkan “afraid of” bersama benda yang kamu takuti. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: We say “takut dengan”, but English uses afraid of.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I am afraid with dogs.” 😅 For fear, use of: “I am afraid of dogs.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: At! He is good at football.

native.tip: Kita bilang “jago dalam”, tapi di bahasa Inggris pakai good at.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I am good in cooking.” 😅 Untuk keahlian, pakai at: “I am good at cooking.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “at”. Bilang “I am good at ...” untuk kemampuanmu. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: We say “jago dalam”, but English uses good at.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I am good in cooking.” 😅 For a skill, use at: “I am good at cooking.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: I am late because of traffic.
in.answer_say: Because of! I am late because of the rain.

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia cukup “karena”, tapi sebelum kata benda bahasa Inggris pakai because of.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I am late because traffic.” 😅 Sebelum kata benda, pakai because of: “I am late because of traffic.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “because of”. Ceritakan alasanmu terlambat dengan because of. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “karena” is enough, but before a noun English uses because of.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I am late because traffic.” 😅 Before a noun, use because of: “I am late because of traffic.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Discuss! Let's discuss the problem.

native.tip: Kita bilang “diskusi tentang”, tapi discuss langsung diikuti topiknya, tanpa about.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “We discussed about the plan.” 😅 Setelah discuss, langsung topiknya: “We discussed the plan.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “discuss”. Bilang “Let's discuss ...” tanpa about. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: We say “diskusi tentang”, but discuss takes the topic directly, with no about.
en.caption: Ever say this? “We discussed about the plan.” 😅 After discuss, go straight to the topic: “We discussed the plan.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I go to office by bus.
in.right: I go to the office by bus.
in.answer_say: The office! I walk to the office every day.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia tidak punya artikel seperti the, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh the sebelum tempat tertentu.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I go to office by bus.” 😅 Sebelum tempat tertentu, pakai the: “I go to the office by bus.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “the office”. Ceritakan perjalananmu: “I go to the ...” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian has no article like the, but English needs the before a specific place.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I go to office by bus.” 😅 Before a specific place, use the: “I go to the office by bus.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Quickly! She speaks quickly now.

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “lancar” tetap, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai -ly untuk kata kerja: fluently. (Bisa: I speak fluent English.)
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I speak English fluent.” 😅 Untuk menjelaskan kata kerja, pakai fluently: “I speak English fluently.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “quickly”. Coba bilang “I speak English slowly”, lalu fluently. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “lancar” stays the same, but English uses -ly for verbs: fluently. (Also OK: I speak fluent English.)
en.caption: Ever say this? “I speak English fluent.” 😅 To describe a verb, use fluently: “I speak English fluently.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: Can you, not do you can!
in.answer_say: Can you! Can you speak English?

native.tip: “Apakah kamu bisa” tampak cocok dengan do you can, tapi di bahasa Inggris can sendiri yang dipindah ke depan.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “Do you can speak English?” 😅 Untuk bertanya bisa, mulai dengan can: “Can you speak English?” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “Can you”. Tanya temanmu: “Can you ...?” Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Apakah kamu bisa” seems to fit do you can, but English moves can to the front by itself.
en.caption: Ever say this? “Do you can speak English?” 😅 To ask about ability, start with can: “Can you speak English?” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Do! I do not know.

native.tip: “Saya tidak mengerti” bukan I am not understand. Understand itu kata kerja, jadi negatifnya pakai don't: I don't understand.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I am not understand.” 😅 Untuk kalimat negatif dengan kata kerja, pakai do not: “I don't understand.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “do”. Latih “I do not understand” dengan tenang. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Saya tidak mengerti” is not I am not understand. Understand is a verb, so its negative uses don't: I don't understand.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I am not understand.” 😅 To make a verb negative, use do not: “I don't understand.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Cheaper! My bag is cheaper.

native.tip: “Lebih murah” jadi more cheaper, padahal -er sudah berarti lebih.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “This bag is more cheaper.” 😅 Cukup cheaper, tanpa more: “This bag is cheaper.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “cheaper”. Bandingkan dua barang dengan -er. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Lebih murah” turns into more cheaper, but -er already means more.
en.caption: Ever say this? “This bag is more cheaper.” 😅 Just cheaper, without more: “This bag is cheaper.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: The same as, not same with!
in.wrong: My phone is same with yours.
in.right: My phone is the same as yours.
in.answer_say: The same as! Her bag is the same as mine.

native.tip: “Sama dengan” bukan same with. Bahasa Inggris pakai the same as.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “My phone is same with yours.” 😅 Untuk menyamakan, pakai the same as: “My phone is the same as yours.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “the same as”. Bandingkan barangmu dengan milik teman pakai the same as. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Sama dengan” is not same with. English uses the same as.
en.caption: Ever say this? “My phone is same with yours.” 😅 To say two things match, use the same as: “My phone is the same as yours.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: For! I am waiting for the bus.

native.tip: Kita bilang “menunggu kamu”, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai wait for.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “I am waiting you.” 😅 Setelah wait, pakai for: “I am waiting for you.” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “for”. Bilang “I am waiting for ...” ke temanmu. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: We say “menunggu kamu”, but English uses wait for.
en.caption: Ever say this? “I am waiting you.” 😅 After wait, use for: “I am waiting for you.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: My mother is a nurse. He works hard.
in.right: My mother is a nurse. She works hard.
in.answer_say: He! My father is tall. He is 40.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia pakai “dia” untuk semua, tapi bahasa Inggris membedakan he dan she.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “My mother is a nurse. He works hard.” 😅 Untuk perempuan pakai she, untuk laki-laki he: “My mother is a nurse. She works hard.” Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “He”. Ceritakan keluargamu dengan he dan she yang tepat. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian uses “dia” for everyone, but English separates he and she.
en.caption: Ever say this? “My mother is a nurse. He works hard.” 😅 For a woman use she, for a man he: “My mother is a nurse. She works hard.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
